problem: Perception models pretrained on Internet images (e.g., COCO Mask R-CNN) make false positives and false negatives on an embodied agent's egocentric views. Prior ways to improve them either need human labels (active learning with an oracle), work on pre-collected passive data (self-training, video consistency), or use exploration policies that are not designed to gather data useful for self-supervised labelling.
motivation: An embodied agent sees a 3D-consistent world from many viewpoints, unlike sparse, unrelated Internet snapshots. Spatio-temporal consistency could therefore supply labels without humans, and the agent can choose which views to collect. The paper asks whether an agent can bootstrap from Internet-pretrained detectors and improve them just by moving around, and whether the improved perception then helps a downstream navigation task.
key_idea: Train an exploration policy with a 'Gainful Curiosity' reward, i.e., the count of 3D semantic-map voxels with confidence >0.9, so it finds objects and gets at least one confident view of each. Aggregate the detector's predictions into a voxel 3D semantic map and ray-trace the thresholded map back into every frame (3DLabelProp) to produce pseudo-labels for fine-tuning Mask R-CNN.
insight: One confident viewpoint per object, fused in 3D and propagated to all other views, fixes per-frame false negatives and false positives. This works far better than per-frame self-training or optical-flow propagation over consecutive frames. The ablation (Table 2) shows the Perception phase is the critical piece: replacing 3DLabelProp with Self-training or Optical Flow drops Generalization detection AP50 to 35.35/35.65, near the pretrained 34.82. Replacing the Gainful Curiosity policy with Active Neural SLAM or Semantic Curiosity only drops it to 38.90/38.39, versus 40.02 for full SEAL. A random policy with 3DLabelProp gives only 35.43 and 31.22 mask AP50, so action still matters. In the weak-supervision extension, 10 entropy-selected labelled frames propagated through the 3D map give 42.63/38.48 AP50, while naive fine-tuning on those 10 frames gives 35.14/32.52.
method: 3D Semantic Mapping: voxel map (5 cm voxels) with K=C+1 channels (occupancy + C=6 category scores). Per-pixel max Mask R-CNN scores are attached to a depth point cloud, transformed to geocentric coordinates with the pose sensor, and aggregated over time by channel-wise max pooling.

Gainful Curiosity reward: the number of map voxels whose score exceeds ŝ=0.9 for at least one category. It rewards seeing new objects and getting confident views of them, rather than maximizing uncertainty as prediction-error curiosity or semantic curiosity do.

Modular exploration policy: a Global Policy (2×3D conv + 3×2D conv + 3 FC, orientation embedding) takes the 3D semantic map and outputs a long-term x-y goal every 25 steps. It is trained with PPO (25 threads, 10M frames, Adam lr 2.5e-5). A deterministic Fast Marching Method local planner executes low-level actions.

3DLabelProp: each voxel is assigned its max-score category if above 0.9, else background. Connected components of same-category voxels become instances; holes <0.25 m³ are filled and objects <0.025 m³ removed. Per-pixel instance labels, masks and boxes for every frame are obtained by ray-tracing the labelled map from the agent's pose.
Perception fine-tuning: COCO-pretrained Mask R-CNN (R50-FPN, Detectron2) is fine-tuned on the self-labelled trajectories with SGD, lr 1e-4, 5000 iterations.

Settings: Generalization trains on 25 Gibson training scenes and tests directly on unseen scenes. Specialization additionally allows one self-supervised 300-step exploration episode per test scene before testing.

Downstream ObjectNav: the SEAL-improved Mask R-CNN replaces the pretrained one inside SemExp, with everything else unchanged. A weak-supervision extension replaces predictions on k highest-entropy frames with human labels (score 1).

setting.backbone: Mask R-CNN R50-FPN (COCO-pretrained, fine-tuned on self-supervised 3DLabelProp labels) + CNN Global Policy trained with PPO; downstream ObjectNav uses SemExp with the SEAL perception model swapped in
setting.training_data: 25 Gibson tiny training scenes in Habitat. Exploration policy: 10M frames of RL with an intrinsic reward and no labels. Mask R-CNN: fine-tuned on single-episode trajectories per training scene, self-labelled via 3D map ray-tracing; Specialization adds one 300-step episode per test scene. No human annotations, except the weak-supervision extension (k=5/10 labelled frames per test scene).
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth + 3-DOF pose sensor (x, y, orientation)
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 30° (FMM local planner) driven by global-policy long-term map goals every 25 steps
setting.privileged: Ground-truth pose sensor (noise-free 3-DOF pose) used for mapping; no GT semantics or maps. The Specialization setting additionally uses one self-supervised 300-step exploration episode in each test scene.

The ObjectNav eval follows SemExp's Gibson val setup and is assumed to use the full episode set, but episode counts are not restated. Perception results are on a custom 2500-image test set, not a standard benchmark.
results: SEAL raises Mask R-CNN AP50 from 34.82/32.54 (box/mask) to 40.02/36.23 in Generalization and 41.23/37.28 in Specialization, without any labels. The strongest baseline combinations reach only 35.85/32.57 (Generalization) and 35.90/33.29 (Specialization), mostly Active Neural SLAM or Semantic Curiosity with optical-flow propagation. Plugging the improved detector into SemExp raises Gibson ObjectNav from 0.544 SR / 0.199 SPL to 0.611/0.323 (Gen.) and 0.627/0.331 (Spec.).
limitations: Label quality is bounded by the pretrained detector: objects never confidently detected from any view cannot be learned, and confident wrong predictions get amplified by 3D label propagation.
Small-scale evaluation: 30 Gibson scenes (25 train / 5 test), 6 object categories, and a custom 2500-image perception test set.
Assumes static scenes and accurate depth plus noise-free pose for 3D map fusion and ray-tracing.
builds_on: SemExp (Object Goal Navigation using Goal-Oriented Semantic Exploration)
compares_to: Active Neural SLAM + Self-training / Optical Flow
